topics.topic: The objective eligibility rule for treating a constant-table row as contract-only with no independent product meaning
questions: What exact criterion determines whether a constant-table row has no product meaning of its own, especially when the row expresses a correspondence between two vocabulary members?
What objective rule determines whether the relationship represented by a table row has no product meaning and therefore may lack a State 1 model record?
What exact, mechanically decidable condition establishes that a row has “no product meaning of its own,” especially when the row embodies a correspondence used by a product rule?

quotes: A row of a constant table may be declared by the contracts alone (`contract_only`), with no record of its own here, when each of its fields names a fact a model here already lists and the row itself has no product meaning of its own; its declaration names where the product rule the table serves is fixed.
judgement.why: The semantic test is stated, but the texts supply no concrete row other than ConfirmedOwnerAction whose classification remains open, so no admissible product history can witness two observable outcomes from the alleged ambiguity.

topics.topic: Whether ConfirmedOwnerAction is runtime or specification data, including its kind, identity, creator, and provenance
questions: Is ConfirmedOwnerAction a runtime value or entity, who creates its rows, and from which facts is each row's identity derived?
What model kind and identity does ConfirmedOwnerAction have, and who creates its runtime instances from what source?

The passage must require every contract-only table-row runtime model either to declare `identity: "value"|"entity"` or to declare one of the registered non-runtime `kind` values; it cannot leave the row only in contracts without either classification.
Is ConfirmedOwnerAction a runtime product model instantiated as each table row, or only the structural row shape of read-only specification data?
If ConfirmedOwnerAction is a runtime model, is its identity value or entity, who creates its instances, and from what authoritative inputs?

quotes: A row of a constant table may be declared by the contracts alone (`contract_only`), with no record of its own here, when each of its fields names a fact a model here already lists and the row itself has no product meaning of its own; its declaration names where the product rule the table serves is fixed.

`ConfirmedOwnerAction`, the row of the data provider's `CONFIRMED_OWNER_ACTIONS`, is one: its two fields name the confirmed action (M20, M31) and the owner action (M27), and the rule the table serves — an action that asks for confirmation is submitted with the confirmation value the step showed — is fixed by State 2 A13 rule 6 and the `ConfirmedAction` vocabulary, the closed list of the actions that ask for confirmation ("Identity formats"). It has no model number here.
judgement.why: The text identifies ConfirmedOwnerAction as the row shape delivered by a provider constant but deliberately leaves it without either a runtime identity declaration or a registered non-runtime kind.
judgement.rule:
Каждая runtime-модель без `kind` обязана объявлять
  `identity: "value"|"entity"`; модели с `kind` поле `identity` не содержат.

topics.topic: The authoritative source and conflict precedence for confirmed-action correspondence

questions: What are the exact ConfirmedAction members, and which OwnerAction does each member correspond to in CONFIRMED_OWNER_ACTIONS?
Which exact confirmed action is paired with which owner action, and must every ConfirmedAction have exactly one row?

quotes: `ConfirmedOwnerAction`, the row of the data provider's `CONFIRMED_OWNER_ACTIONS`, is one: its two fields name the confirmed action (M20, M31) and the owner action (M27), and the rule the table serves — an action that asks for confirmation is submitted with the confirmation value the step showed — is fixed by State 2 A13 rule 6 and the `ConfirmedAction` vocabulary, the closed list of the actions that ask for confirmation ("Identity formats"). It has no model number here.

The confirmation id is a UUID. Registry mints a confirmation id when the owner confirms an action that asks for confirmation — archiving a project, erasing an archived project, the import, erasing old audit entries (Primary actions) — and writes it once into the audit entry of that action (M09) and, for the import, into the migration closure (M10).

judgement.divergence: One implementation supplies exactly one row pairing each of archive-project, erase-project, confirm-import and erase-audit-entries with its corresponding OwnerAction, while another omits a row or pairs a ConfirmedAction with a different OwnerAction; the owner observes whether the submitted action is accepted, refused, or guarded by the wrong confirmation.
judgement.why: The texts enumerate the confirmation-requiring actions and require runtime lookup through CONFIRMED_OWNER_ACTIONS, but neither they nor the later texts state the rows or require exactly one row for every ConfirmedAction.

witness.initial: An owner session holds a pending confirmation value shown for archiving a project.
events: Registry shows the owner a confirmation step for archiving the project.

outcomes: With a unique archive-project-to-archive-project row, Registry consumes the confirmation and runs the archive action.

With the row omitted or paired to another owner action, Registry does not apply that confirmation requirement to the archive submission or checks it against a different confirmed action, changing acceptance and execution.
basis: The confirmation step an owner session shows and waits on (M11; State 2 A13 rule 6, A16 rule 2): what the owner is asked to confirm and what the confirmation will be checked against. At most one per session.

The confirmation id is a UUID. Registry mints a confirmation id when the owner confirms an action that asks for confirmation — archiving a project, erasing an archived project, the import, erasing old audit entries (Primary actions) — and writes it once into the audit entry of that action (M09) and, for the import, into the migration closure (M10).

An action that asks for confirmation (Identity formats) is submitted with a
   confirmation value Registry made when it showed the step: one-time, kept in
   the owner session, bound to the action, its target, the revision or access
   version the step showed, or that it showed none when the action has
   neither (a record without a revision, A04 rule 3, among them), and its
   inputs — for the import, the file's digest
   and the picks: a submission whose action, target, version or inputs
   differ from those the step showed is refused (test 12).

author_guidance: Before editing, identify the decision's owning state from the phase purpose, question_scope and layer obligations, then choose a disposition for each topic that awaits one.
fixed: repair a decision the owning state must make; do not add later-layer implementation choices merely to close a topic. Record the fix commit and review the changed text once.

carried: name the receiving layer and use --what to preserve the choice, its options and consequences, and the required guarantee every option must keep. Decide any guarantee owned here before carrying its execution onward.
accepted: explain why the remaining choice is permitted. Bring an unresolved product choice to the owner with its options and consequences; absence of a quoted requirement does not decide it.
contradiction and standard_violation take no disposition: repair the offending text in its owning state and review the change. Deterministic transition findings must also close through their checks.
